newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins higher on long-awaited Eurobond.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins higher on long-awaited Eurobond.

text.p: Russian MinFin bonds rose on Thursday amid optimism about Russia's new Eurobond and Moscow's plans to close an agreement with the London Club of commercial creditors, dealers said.
But they said the rise was muted by weaker U.S. Treasuries.
"The market is still strong, but we could see some profit-taking today," Eurobank dealer Olivier Coursault said. "The Eurobond issue is long-awaited and could not push up prices at these levels."

Russia raised $2.0 billion, twice the amount originally expected, in the international capital markets with the launch of a 10-year Eurobond. Dealers said earlier MinFin prices had firmed briefly by 0.25-0.40 points after the news.
Dealers said Thursday's U.S. mixed statistics was another braking factor for MinFins.
"Figures on jobless claims were good for U.S. interest rates but there was some disappointment with the Philadelphia survey," Coursault said.
The U.S. Labour Department said on Thursday that weekly jobless claims rose to 347,000 in the week ended June 14. Claims stood at 339,000 the week before.
U.S. Stocks and bonds eased after the Philadelphia Federal Reserve's June business activity index came in at 25.2, up from 1.6 in May. Economists had expected a reading of 7.3.
MinFins, like other emerging debt, are sensitive to any news which would suggest a change in U.S. interest rates and consequently affect U.S. Treasury bond prices.
Dealers said news that Russia plans to close an agreement with the London Club of commercial bank creditors by August 15, 1997, was also widely anticipated and had little impact on prices.

"This kind of news could have been bullish if it had come out in the middle of July," Coursault said. "But we are now in the period of position-squaring ahead of half-year and we can see some profit-taking for this reason."
